title: Multi-Partner Project: Securing Future Edge-AI Processors in Practice (CONVOLVE)
problem: Edge-AI devices have limited computing and energy resources yet require high performance and security. Attackers with physical access can target cryptographic keys and neural network weights (IP), creating multiple attack vectors.
motivation: Market for Smart Edge Processors (SEPs) will grow beyond 70 Billion USD by 2026, but edge devices must balance performance, energy, and security under physical attack threat models.
method: CONVOLVE follows a holistic approach combining novel hardware technologies, end-to-end integrated workflows, and security-by-design methodology. Addresses challenges of computing resources, energy efficiency, and multi-vector security threats.
key_novelty: Comprehensive security-by-design framework for low-power edge-AI processors addressing both cryptographic and neural network IP protection under physical attack constraints.
contributions: Holistic approach to edge-AI processor security and efficiency
Address cryptographic key and neural network weight protection
primary_theme: Secure, low-power edge-AI processor design and systems
